title: Finite Weyl Invariants, Bruhat Order, and Kostant Harmonics

items.title: Finite Weyl root system, lattice and chamber conventions

references.title: Pavel Etingof, Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, §§21–22; local sign-change proofs fill the chamber argument

items.statement:
Let $E$ be a finite-dimensional real vector space with a positive definite symmetric bilinear form $(\ ,\ )$. A **finite reduced crystallographic root system** is a finite subset $\Phi\subseteq E\setminus\{0\}$ spanning $E$, such that for every $\alpha,\beta\in\Phi$ the integer $\langle\beta,\alpha^\vee\rangle=2(\beta,\alpha)/(\alpha,\alpha)$ is integral, the reflection $s_\alpha(x)=x-\langle x,\alpha^\vee\rangle\alpha$ preserves $\Phi$, and the only scalar multiples of $\alpha$ in $\Phi$ are $\alpha,-\alpha$. The **Weyl group** $W$ is the subgroup of linear isometries of $E$ generated by these reflections. A **root reflection** means one of the $s_\alpha$. The empty root system on $E=0$ is allowed, with $W=\{1\}$.

Choose $t\in E$ such that $(t,\alpha)\ne0$ for every root. Put $\Phi^+=\{\alpha:(t,\alpha)>0\}$ and $\Phi^-=-\Phi^+$. A positive root is **simple** if it is not the sum of two positive roots. The following positive-root lemma proves that the simple roots form a basis $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_r$ and that the simple reflections $s_i=s_{\alpha_i}$ generate $W$; no such assertion is assumed by this definition. Once proved, let $\ell(w)$ be the least number of simple reflections in a word for $w$ and let $\operatorname{Inv}(w)=\{\alpha\in\Phi^+:w\alpha\in\Phi^-\}$. A word is reduced if its length equals $\ell(w)$.

Identify $E$ with its dual by the displayed form, so $\alpha^\vee=2\alpha/(\alpha,\alpha)$. The root and coroot groups are $Q=\sum_{\alpha\in\Phi}\mathbb Z\alpha$ and $Q^\vee=\sum_{\alpha\in\Phi}\mathbb Z\alpha^\vee$. The **weight group** is $P=\{\lambda\in E:(\lambda,\alpha^\vee)\in\mathbb Z\text{ for all }\alpha\in\Phi\}$; the positive-root lemma proves it is a lattice with basis the vectors dual to the simple coroots. Put $Q_+=\sum_i\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\alpha_i$, and write $\mu\le\lambda$ when $\lambda-\mu\in Q_+$. The open and closed positive chambers are $\mathcal C=\{x:(x,\alpha_i)>0\text{ for all }i\}$ and $\overline{\mathcal C}=\{x:(x,\alpha_i)\ge0\text{ for all }i\}$. A weight is dominant if it belongs to $P\cap\overline{\mathcal C}$. More generally chambers are the connected components of $E\setminus\bigcup_{\alpha\in\Phi}\alpha^\perp$. The closed-chamber representative and stabilizer assertions are proved later, not included as axioms.

items.title: Finite Weyl positive roots and simple reflections

references.title: Pavel Etingof, Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, §§21–22; local sign-change proofs fill the chamber argument

items.statement: For the preceding finite reduced crystallographic root system, regular vectors $t$ exist, $W$ is finite, and the simple positive roots are a basis of $E$. Every root has integral coordinates in this basis of one sign. Each $s_i$ permutes $\Phi^+\setminus\{\alpha_i\}$ and sends $\alpha_i$ to $-\alpha_i$. The simple reflections generate $W$, and every root is the image of a simple root under their group. The simple coroots similarly form an integral basis of the coroot group, and $P$ is the lattice generated by their dual basis; $W$ preserves $Q,Q^\vee,P$. All assertions are choice-free, including rank zero.

items.title: Finite weyl strong exchange and deletion
items.statement:
For the simple reflections of a finite reduced crystallographic root system, word length equals inversion length: $\ell(w)=|\operatorname{Inv}(w)|$. If a root reflection $t$ satisfies $\ell(tw)<\ell(w)$, every reduced word for $w$ loses exactly one letter to give $tw$. Every nonreduced word admits deletion of two letters without changing its group element.

More precisely, for $\beta\in\Phi^+$, $\ell(s_\beta w)<\ell(w)$ if and only if $w^{-1}\beta<0$. In this case one letter can be deleted from any word for $w$ to give $s_\beta w$, although the resulting word need not be reduced. Also $\ell(ws_i)=\ell(w)\pm1$, with the minus sign exactly when $w\alpha_i<0$. These are assertions for the geometric reflection group, without an assumed Coxeter presentation or exchange axiom.

items.title: Finite Weyl closed chambers and stabilizers

references.title: Pavel Etingof, Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, §§21–22; local sign-change proofs fill the chamber argument

items.statement: Every $W$-orbit in $E$ has exactly one point in $\overline{\mathcal C}$. For $\eta\in\overline{\mathcal C}$, its stabilizer is generated by those simple reflections $s_i$ with $(\eta,\alpha_i)=0$. The group acts simply transitively on open chambers. There is a unique longest element $w_0$, characterized by $w_0\Phi^+=\Phi^-$; it has length $|\Phi^+|$ and satisfies $w_0^2=1$. In particular every weight orbit has a unique dominant weight. These assertions include rank zero and singular wall points, without AC.

items.title: Bruhat order on a finite weyl group
items.statement:
For the geometric finite Weyl group and its simple reflections, define $u\le v$ when a reduced expression for $v$ contains a reduced expression for $u$ as an ordered subword: choose positions in increasing order, multiply their letters in that order, and require their number to be $\ell(u)$. The empty subword represents the identity.

The following proof shows this condition is independent of the reduced expression for $v$ and is equivalent to a chain $u=w_0,w_1,\ldots,w_k=v$ with $w_{j+1}=t_jw_j$, each $t_j$ a root reflection and $\ell(w_{j+1})=\ell(w_j)+1$. Thus it is a partial order, called **strong Bruhat order**. A zero-length chain is allowed. The subword and saturated-reflection-chain descriptions are proved equivalent here; neither an abstract Coxeter presentation nor weak order or inversion-set containment is being substituted.
items.strategy: Complete four-case saturated-edge lifting proof, then induction from subwords to chains and reverse strong-exchange deletions for every reduced expression.
items.purpose: Well-defined strong Bruhat order proved for the actual geometric finite Weyl group with local root suppliers; original exhausted BB fetch history remains.

items.title: Weyl orbit sum in a group algebra
items.statement:
Use the finite reduced crystallographic root system and weight lattice $P$ of [[def-finite-weyl-root-system-lattice-and-chamber-conventions]], with the proved finite $W$ action and lattice preservation of [[lem-finite-weyl-positive-roots-and-simple-reflections]]. The complex group algebra $\mathbb C[P]$ consists of finitely supported sums $\sum_{\mu\in P}c_\mu e^\mu$, with formal basis indexed by $P$ and multiplication $e^\mu e^\nu=e^{\mu+\nu}$ extended distributively. Finite supports make each product finite, and the abelian group law of $P$ proves associativity and commutativity; $e^0$ is the unit. The action $w(e^\mu)=e^{w\mu}$ extends to algebra automorphisms because $w$ is additive and permutes $P$.

For $\lambda\in P$ define the **orbit sum** $m_\lambda=\sum_{\mu\in W\lambda}e^\mu$, summing each distinct orbit element once. The orbit is finite and nonempty, and $W$ permutes it, so $m_\lambda\in\mathbb C[P]^W$. Stabilizers do not multiply coefficients. In particular $m_0=e^0=1$. For rank zero, $P=\{0\}$ and this is the one-dimensional algebra $\mathbb C$. No choice of representatives for a family of orbits is part of the definition.

items.title: Weyl orbit sums form a basis of finite weyl invariants
items.statement:
Orbit sums indexed by the distinct $W$-orbits in $P$ form a complex vector-space basis of $\mathbb C[P]^W$. Equivalently they are indexed by dominant integral weights, with exactly one per orbit, including weights on chamber walls. Every invariant has finite support in this basis.

For each dominant $\lambda$, the set of dominant $\mu\le\lambda$ is finite. In fact every such $\mu$ satisfies $\|\mu\|\le\|\lambda\|$ for the specified invariant Euclidean norm. All assertions are choice-free.

items.statement: For distinct finite G-orbits O1,O2 in V over C there is an invariant polynomial taking value zero on O1 and one on O2.
items.strategy: For each b in O2 and a in O1 choose a linear functional l with l(b-a)!=0 using a nonzero coordinate. Multiply l(x-a)/l(b-a) over a in O1 to vanish on O1 and equal one at b. Finite interpolation on O1 union O2 is cleaner: for each b form delta_b using a separating linear factor for every other point. Sum delta_b over O2, then Reynolds-average. All points of an orbit have the required value, so averaging preserves it. Stabilizers cause no overcount because interpolate distinct points and divide by |G|. Empty target constraints allow constants. Finite choices only.

items.title: Weyl discriminant and reflecting hyperplane arrangement
items.statement:
Use the finite root system, $W$ and $\Phi^+$ of [[def-finite-weyl-root-system-lattice-and-chamber-conventions]], complexify to $V=E\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C$, and write $S=\mathbb C[V]$ with the action $(w\cdot p)(v)=p(w^{-1}v)$ of [[def-finite-linear-invariant-and-coinvariant-polynomial-algebras]]. For each root let $\ell_\alpha(v)=(\alpha,v)$, extending the Euclidean form complex bilinearly. The **reflecting arrangement** is the collection of distinct hyperplanes $\ker\ell_\alpha$ for $\alpha\in\Phi^+$. The **Weyl discriminant** is
$$\Delta=\prod_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}\ell_\alpha\in S.$$
Reducedness makes these factors pairwise nonproportional, so its degree is the number of these hyperplanes. In rank zero the product is $1$ and the arrangement is empty. The following argument verifies that these are exactly the reflection hyperplanes of $W$, and that $w\cdot\Delta=\det(w)\Delta$.

items.title: Weyl anti invariants are divisible by the discriminant
items.statement:
For the finite Weyl reflection action on $S=\mathbb C[V]$, put $S^{\det}=\{p:w\cdot p=\det(w)p\text{ for all }w\in W\}$. Then
$$S^{\det}=\Delta S^W.$$
The invariant quotient is unique. This includes rank zero and the zero polynomial, and is choice-free.

items.title: Finite semisimple Lie algebras and the symmetric adjoint action

references.title: Pavel Etingof, Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, §§15–17; finite-dimensional local trace proof

items.statement:
A finite-dimensional complex **Lie algebra** is a finite-dimensional complex vector space $\mathfrak g$ with a complex bilinear bracket satisfying $[x,x]=0$ and $[x,[y,z]]+[y,[z,x]]+[z,[x,y]]=0$. A subspace $I$ is an ideal if $[\mathfrak g,I]\subseteq I$. Put $D^0\mathfrak g=\mathfrak g$ and $D^{j+1}\mathfrak g=[D^j\mathfrak g,D^j\mathfrak g]$, where a bracket of subspaces means the span of all indicated brackets. The algebra is **solvable** if some $D^j\mathfrak g=0$, and **semisimple** if it has no nonzero solvable ideal. The zero algebra is semisimple. The operator $\operatorname{ad}_x(y)=[x,y]$ satisfies $[\operatorname{ad}_x,\operatorname{ad}_y]=\operatorname{ad}_{[x,y]}$ by Jacobi. Its **Killing form** is $B(x,y)=\operatorname{tr}_{\mathfrak g}(\operatorname{ad}_x\operatorname{ad}_y)$; its nondegeneracy in the semisimple case is proved in the next lemma, not assumed here.

The symmetric algebra $S(\mathfrak g)$ is the commutative algebra generated linearly by $\mathfrak g$. Concretely, a finite vector-space basis $e_1,\ldots,e_n$ identifies it with the polynomial algebra $\mathbb C[e_1,\ldots,e_n]$ of [[def-polynomial-ring-over-a-commutative-ring]]. A change of basis induces an invertible linear substitution, so these descriptions identify canonically by their values on $\mathfrak g$. Its grading $S=\bigoplus_{d\ge0}S_d$ has $S_0=\mathbb C$. Each $\operatorname{ad}_x$ extends uniquely to a derivation of $S$ by the product rule, and the Lie identities continue to hold because derivations are determined by their values on generators. Define $S^{\mathfrak g}=\{p:\operatorname{ad}_x p=0\text{ for every }x\in\mathfrak g\}$ and $S^{\mathfrak g}_+=\bigoplus_{d>0}(S^{\mathfrak g}\cap S_d)$. The invariant ideal $I=S S^{\mathfrak g}_+$ consists of finite sums of products with positive-degree homogeneous invariants; it is graded and stable under all adjoint derivations. In dimension zero, $S=S^{\mathfrak g}=\mathbb C$ and $I=0$. Only finite basis choices occur in these conventions.

references.title: Pavel Etingof, Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, §§15–17; finite-dimensional local trace proof

items.statement:
Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex vector space. If a Lie subalgebra $L\subseteq\operatorname{End}(V)$ consists entirely of nilpotent operators and $V\ne0$, it has a common nonzero annihilated vector; it admits a basis in which all its operators are strictly upper triangular. If instead $L$ satisfies $\operatorname{tr}_V(xy)=0$ for all $x\in[L,L]$, $y\in L$, then $L$ is solvable.

For every finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra, the Killing form $B$ is symmetric, invariant and nondegenerate. All these assertions are choice-free, including the zero Lie algebra.

items.title: Finite Lie triangularization and rank-one complete reducibility
items.statement:
Every representation of a finite-dimensional solvable complex Lie algebra on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex vector space has a common eigenvector; in a suitable basis all its operators are upper triangular.

Every finite-dimensional complex representation of the relations $[h,e]=2e$, $[h,f]=-2f$, $[e,f]=h$ is a finite direct sum of the simple modules $V_m$, $m\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$. The module $V_m$ has basis $v_0,\ldots,v_m$ and action
$$h v_k=(m-2k)v_k,\qquad f v_k=v_{k+1},\qquad e v_k=k(m-k+1)v_{k-1},$$
where missing endpoint vectors are zero. In particular $h$ is diagonalizable with integral eigenvalues and $e,f$ are nilpotent. On $V_m$, $fe$ acts at index $k$ by $k(m-k+1)$ and $ef$ by $(k+1)(m-k)$; the latter is strictly positive when $0\le k<m$. The zero representation is the empty sum. All assertions are choice-free.

items.title: Finite semisimple Cartan, root and string structure
items.statement:
Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra with Killing form $B$. A **Cartan subalgebra** here means a maximal toral subalgebra: a maximal abelian subalgebra $\mathfrak h$ all of whose adjoint operators are diagonalizable. Such subalgebras exist, and every one is self-centralizing. There is a decomposition
$$\mathfrak g=\mathfrak h\oplus\bigoplus_{\alpha\in\Phi}\mathfrak g_\alpha,\qquad \mathfrak g_\alpha=\{x:[h,x]=\alpha(h)x\text{ for all }h\in\mathfrak h\},$$
where the nonzero weights $\Phi$ are finite, span $\mathfrak h^*$, and each root space has dimension one. The form is nondegenerate on $\mathfrak h$, pairs $\mathfrak g_\alpha$ perfectly with $\mathfrak g_{-\alpha}$, and all other weight-space pairings are zero. Define $H_\alpha\in\mathfrak h$ by $B(H_\alpha,h)=\alpha(h)$. Then $c_\alpha=\alpha(H_\alpha)\ne0$, and $h_\alpha=2H_\alpha/c_\alpha$ admits root vectors $e_\alpha,f_\alpha$ with $[e_\alpha,f_\alpha]=h_\alpha$, $[h_\alpha,e_\alpha]=2e_\alpha$, $[h_\alpha,f_\alpha]=-2f_\alpha$.

The real span $\mathfrak h_{\mathbb R}$ of the $h_\alpha$ is a real form of $\mathfrak h$ on which $B$ is positive definite. On $E=\mathfrak h_{\mathbb R}^*$ with the dual form, $\Phi$ is a finite reduced crystallographic root system and $h_\alpha$ is its coroot. In particular the preceding abstract finite-Weyl conventions apply. For nonproportional roots $\alpha,\beta$, the root spaces with roots $\beta+k\alpha$ form one simple rank-one module: the integers occurring are a consecutive interval, reflection in $\alpha$ reverses it, and raising or lowering between adjacent spaces is nonzero with the positive $fe,ef$ coefficients of $V_m$. The adjoint operators of all root vectors are nilpotent. For any positive system, normalized triples $e_i,f_i,h_i$ of its simple roots generate $\mathfrak g$, and the $h_i$ form a basis of $\mathfrak h$. All assertions include $\mathfrak g=0$ and use no AC.
items.strategy: Internal Jordan parts, maximal toral centralizer, rank-one strings and the real Killing form prove finite root structure locally.
items.purpose: Supplies the finite semisimple root and simple-generator interfaces without later PBW, GCM or Harish-Chandra dependencies.

items.title: Finite semisimple PBW and highest-weight construction
items.statement:
For a finite-dimensional complex Lie algebra $\mathfrak a$, its **universal enveloping algebra** is $U(\mathfrak a)=T(\mathfrak a)/(xy-yx-[x,y])$, where $T$ is the algebra of finite linear combinations of finite tensor words, including the empty word $1$, and the denominator is the two-sided ideal generated by the displayed relations. For any ordered finite basis $x_1,\ldots,x_n$, the monomials $x_1^{a_1}\cdots x_n^{a_n}$ form a vector-space basis of $U(\mathfrak a)$.

Now let $\mathfrak g$ be finite-dimensional complex semisimple with a Cartan and positive system as in the preceding root-structure lemma. Set $\mathfrak n^\pm=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in\Phi^\pm}\mathfrak g_\alpha$ and $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^+$. For $\lambda\in\mathfrak h^*$ let $\mathbb C_\lambda$ be the one-dimensional $\mathfrak b$-module on which $\mathfrak h$ acts by $\lambda$ and $\mathfrak n^+$ by zero, and define $M(\lambda)=U(\mathfrak g)\otimes_{U(\mathfrak b)}\mathbb C_\lambda$. It is generated by $v_\lambda=1\otimes1$, with $hv_\lambda=\lambda(h)v_\lambda$ and $\mathfrak n^+v_\lambda=0$, and is universal for these relations. Its negative-root ordered monomials on $v_\lambda$ form a basis; its support is $\lambda-Q_+$, each weight space is finite-dimensional and the top space has dimension one. It has a unique simple quotient $L(\lambda)$.

For every dominant integral $\lambda$, $L(\lambda)$ is finite-dimensional, its support is contained in $\lambda-Q_+$, its top weight has multiplicity one, and all its weight multiplicities are $W$-invariant. Every nonzero finite-dimensional simple $\mathfrak g$-module is exactly one such $L(\lambda)$ up to isomorphism, with a unique dominant integral highest weight. These assertions include the zero algebra and use no AC.

items.title: Kostant harmonic subspace of the symmetric algebra
items.statement:
Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra with the symmetric adjoint action of [[def-finite-semisimple-lie-algebra-and-symmetric-adjoint-action]]. Its Killing form $B(x,y)=\operatorname{tr}(\operatorname{ad}_x\operatorname{ad}_y)$ is nondegenerate and invariant by [[lem-finite-lie-engel-trace-criterion-and-killing-nondegeneracy]]. Thus $x\mapsto B(x,\cdot)$ identifies $S(\mathfrak g)$ with polynomial functions on $\mathfrak g$; a finite basis and its Killing-dual basis give inverse linear substitutions.

For $x\in\mathfrak g$ define the constant-coefficient derivation $D_x$ of $S(\mathfrak g)$ by $D_x(y)=B(x,y)$ on generators. These derivations commute, so for $p\in S$ substitution extends multiplicatively and linearly to an operator $D_p=p(\partial)$. Under the polynomial-function identification, $D_x$ is directional differentiation along $x$, since it differentiates $B(y,\cdot)$ to $B(y,x)$. The **Kostant harmonic subspace** is
$$\mathcal H=\{h\in S:D_p h=0\text{ for every }p\in S^{\mathfrak g}_+\}.$$
Equivalently one may test only homogeneous positive-degree invariants, since their finite homogeneous sums exhaust that ideal. This is a graded subspace. With $I=S S^{\mathfrak g}_+$, its degree-$d$ part is the annihilator $I_d^\perp$ for the perfect bilinear Fischer pairing $(p,q)_B=(D_pq)(0)$ on $S_d$, as verified below. It is stable under the adjoint action. The direct-sum complement assertion $S_d=\mathcal H_d\oplus I_d$ is a separate theorem; it is not inferred from complex bilinear nondegeneracy.

items.title: Highest-weight characters are unitriangular in Weyl orbit sums
items.statement:
For a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra with a fixed Cartan and positive system, let $L(\lambda)$ be the finite-dimensional simple module of dominant integral highest weight $\lambda$. Its formal character is $\operatorname{ch}L(\lambda)=\sum_{
u\in P}(\dim L(\lambda)_
u)e^
u\in\mathbb C[P]$. Then
$$\operatorname{ch}L(\lambda)=m_\lambda+\sum_{\substack{\mu	ext{ dominant}\\mu<\lambda}}n_{\lambda,\mu}m_\mu,$$
where the coefficients are nonnegative integers and the support is finite. The inverse expansion expressing $m_\lambda$ in these characters has integral coefficients, coefficient one at $\operatorname{ch}L(\lambda)$, and finite support on the same dominant ideal. In particular the characters form a basis of $\mathbb C[P]^W$. All statements include singular dominant weights and rank zero, without AC.
items.strategy: Use the locally proved finite highest-weight modules and Weyl multiplicity symmetry, then invert the strictly lowering integer matrix on each proved finite dominant ideal.
items.purpose: Exact original character triangularity and finite inverse, without missing or later highest-weight suppliers.

references.title: Pavel Etingof, Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, §§25–26; local orbit-sum triangular inversion

items.title: Kostant harmonics give an invariant polynomial complement
items.statement:
For every finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, let $S=S(\mathfrak g)$, $R=S^{\mathfrak g}$, $I=SR_+$ and let $\mathcal H$ be its Kostant harmonic subspace. Then
$$S_d=\mathcal H_d\oplus I_d\quad(d\ge0),\qquad S=\mathcal H\oplus S S^{\mathfrak g}_+.$$
The splitting is graded and $\mathfrak g$-equivariant. This includes $\mathfrak g=0$ and is choice-free.
items.strategy: Construct the sign conjugation from a local universal quotient and prove positive Killing/Fischer pairings by root-string induction, then split each finite degree.
items.purpose: Complete exact harmonic complement; no ambient complex-bilinear nondegeneracy shortcut and no later compact-form dependency.

references.title: Pavel Etingof, Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, §41.1; local universal sign-conjugation and positive Fischer proof

items.title: Local Chevalley restriction for Kostant freeness
items.statement:
For a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ and any Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$, restriction of polynomial functions gives a graded algebra isomorphism
$$\mathbb C[\mathfrak g]^{\mathfrak g}\longrightarrow\mathbb C[\mathfrak h]^W.$$
Equivalently, under the Killing identifications it is the graded isomorphism $S(\mathfrak g)^{\mathfrak g}\cong S(\mathfrak h)^W$, where restriction on symmetric algebras is the algebra map induced by the Killing-orthogonal projection $\mathfrak g\to\mathfrak h$. This holds also in rank zero and uses no AC.
items.strategy: Finite root exponentials implement Weyl reflections and an invertible-linear-part polynomial density map; trace moments, finite character inversion and an integer-grid coefficient argument prove surjectivity.
items.purpose: Complete exact local restriction theorem without global Cartan conjugacy, analytic inverse function theorem or published restriction consumers.

references.title: Pavel Etingof, Representations of Lie Groups, Theorem10.1 pp54–55; local polynomial-density and finite character proof

items.title: Kostant harmonic decomposition of the symmetric algebra
items.statement: For a complex semisimple Lie algebra g, multiplication S(g)^g tensor H -> S(g) is an isomorphism of graded g-modules.
items.strategy: Use Etingof Theorem13.1 first paragraph only: assign weight2 to Cartan coordinates and weight1 to root coordinates, so the leading terms of invariant generators are their Cartan restrictions. Finite-Weyl freeness makes the associated graded free over those restrictions. Induction on this bounded-below filtration proves freeness before considering harmonic lifts. The degreewise harmonic complement then provides lifts of S/I; graded degree induction gives surjectivity and freeness/Hilbert series gives injectivity. Include the filtered induction inline here since the subsequent general lifting lemma must not be used forwards. The stronger zero-weight multiplicity formula is not part of this design theorem and is not assumed.
items.purpose: Authored from the local harmonic complement, local Chevalley restriction and finite-Weyl freeness. Explicit nonnegative-weight induction proves a graded free basis; the harmonic quotient then gives multiplication bijectivity and equivariance. No published enveloping freeness theorem or later lifting lemma is used.

items.title: Filtered freeness lifts from associated graded algebras
items.statement: Let A be a unital nonnegatively filtered algebra and R a compatibly filtered central subalgebra, with exhaustive filtrations and F(-1)=0. Suppose specified homogeneous elements b_j are a free graded basis of gr A over gr R, and specified lifts a_j in A have these symbols. Then the a_j are a free left and right R-basis of A.
items.strategy: Define the filtered module source as the direct sum of copies of R shifted by deg b_j; every vector has finite support. To span a in F_n A, express its symbol as a finite sum of homogeneous gr R coefficients times b_j, lift coefficients, subtract, and induct on n. The base F_-1=0 terminates. For independence take a nonzero finite relation and its maximal filtration degree among coefficient times lifts. The top symbols give a nontrivial relation among the b_j, impossible; repeat only if all top coefficients vanish, contradicting their chosen exact degrees. Centrality gives right freeness. The basis and its lifts are given as data, so there is no arbitrary basis/lift selection and no AC use. All filtered terminology is explicitly included in the statement/strategy.
items.purpose: Authored Step 3b: Authored four-step shifted-direct-sum proof; degree induction lifts finite coefficients, maximal exact degree proves independence, centrality gives right basis. Explicit empty/zero/degree-zero/singleton and no-AC checks; explicit-path precheck, render and strict item contract pass. No external mathematical supplier is used.

title: Finite Weyl Invariants, Bruhat Order, and Kostant Harmonics: Examples

items.title: S3 bruhat order and inversion sets
items.statement: For A2, S3 has Bruhat ranks {123}, {213,132}, {231,312}, {321}; every element in the first middle rank lies below both in the second. Inversion-set containment does not describe strong Bruhat order.
items.strategy: Write s1=(12),s2=(23) with rightmost permutation acting first. Length2 elements are s1s2=231 and s2s1=312, each containing both simple one-letter subwords. The inversion sets in one-line position convention for s1 and 231 are {(1,2)} and {(1,3),(2,3)}, so s1<=231 although its inversion set is not contained. List all six words and reflect covers.
items.purpose: Authored Step 3b: Fully enumerated all six permutations, all reduced expressions, lower sets, every cover and reflection-chain equivalence, and all inversion sets with explicit failed containment witness. Local six-element well-definedness replaces unavailable general Bruhat dependency. Precheck/render and strict30/30 pass.

references.title: Björner and Brenti, Combinatorics of Coxeter Groups, §2.2; the six-element computation is supplied locally

items.title: A2 coinvariant algebra and basic invariants
items.statement: For S3 acting on x+y+z=0, the invariant ring is C[e2,e3], degrees2,3; the coinvariant Hilbert series is 1+2t+2t^2+t^3 and its dimension is6.
items.strategy: Eliminate z=-x-y: e2=-(x^2+xy+y^2), e3=-xy(x+y). Reduction gives y^2=-x^2-xy and x^3=0. Basis candidates 1,x,y,x^2,xy,x^2y are independent by the monic Groebner reductions y^2+xy+x^2 and x^3 (the only S polynomial reduces to zero). Symmetrize a lift from the plane and use the elementary symmetric leading-monomial induction to prove invariant generation. This verifies rather than assumes the numerical formula.
items.purpose: Authored Step 3b: Explicit symmetric-lift generation, nonzero Jacobian independence, ideal identity and monic iterated quotient proving all six basis classes and Hilbert degrees. Both suppliers read; explicit precheck/render and strict29/29 passed.

references.title: Pavel Etingof, Representations of Lie Groups, §§11–13; local proof and exact reading limits in the group report

items.title: Sl2 kostant harmonic decomposition
items.statement: For sl2, after a complex linear orthogonal coordinate change write q=x^2+y^2+z^2. Then C[x,y,z]=C[q] tensor ker(partial_x^2+partial_y^2+partial_z^2) as graded vector spaces, with harmonic dimension2n+1 in degree n.
items.strategy: Verify the invariant quadratic from the Killing form and identify the invariant ring by the rank-one restriction. For homogeneous harmonic h of degree m, direct differentiation gives Laplacian(q^k h)=2k(2m+2k+1)q^(k-1)h. All coefficients for k>0 are nonzero; induct on degree to split into powers of q times harmonic components. The dimensions telescope binomial(n+2,2)-binomial(n,2)=2n+1 including n=0,1.
items.purpose: Complete local matrix Killing trace, invariant polynomial equations and Laplacian decomposition; no later Harish-Chandra-page definition is consumed.

references.title: Pavel Etingof, Representations of Lie Groups, §§11–13; local proof and exact reading limits in the group report

title: Integrable Highest Weight Kac Moody Modules

items.title: Universal property and pbw character of kac moody verma modules
items.statement: For a finite GCM over C and any weight lambda, M_A(lambda) represents a specified highest vector of weight lambda. It belongs to O and ch M_A(lambda)=e^lambda product over positive roots alpha of (1-e^{-alpha})^{-dim g_alpha}, coefficientwise.
items.strategy: Reuse the exact published induced-module definition: u tensor 1 maps uniquely to uv, as the Borel tensor relations hold. Order the supplied homogeneous negative bases; PBW gives an independent basis of monomials. Define the displayed formal character here as the coefficient function mu -> dim M_mu, without importing RL15 completion. At beta=sum b_i alpha_i, only root degrees with every coordinate at most b_i and finitely many basis elements can occur; all exponents are bounded by height beta. Multiply their geometric series coefficientwise, so the infinite product has a finite coefficient computation. Top coefficient one and lower-cone support prove nonzero and O membership. No arbitrary basis choice: RL12 supplies canonical countably based homogeneous root spaces.
source_locators: Kleshchev Lemma 9.1.1 p117 and Lemma 9.2.4 pp121–122; Perrin Proposition 10.3.2 p86 and Proposition 10.7.5 p91

references.title: Kleshchev, Lectures on Infinite Dimensional Lie Algebras
Perrin, Introduction to Kac-Moody Groups and Lie Algebras

items.title: Kac moody verma module has a unique simple quotient
items.statement: M_A(lambda) has a unique maximal proper submodule and nonzero simple highest-weight quotient L_A(lambda); any simple module with highest weight lambda is that quotient.
items.strategy: Submodules decompose into weights by finite Cartan interpolation. A proper submodule has zero top space because that line generates M. The algebraic sum of all proper submodules still has zero top space, hence is proper and contains every proper submodule. The quotient is simple. Universality identifies any highest-weight simple quotient by its maximal kernel. Do not use a general maximal-submodule Zorn theorem or finite-dimensional Schur lemma.
source_locators: Kleshchev Proposition 9.1.2 p117; Perrin Proposition 10.3.2(iii), Corollary 10.3.3 p86

references.title: Kleshchev, Lectures on Infinite Dimensional Lie Algebras
Perrin, Introduction to Kac-Moody Groups and Lie Algebras

items.title: Kac moody integral and dominant integral weights
items.statement: P={lambda in h*: lambda(h_i) in Z for all i} and Pplus={lambda in P: lambda(h_i)>=0 for all i}; values on complementary Cartan directions remain arbitrary complex numbers.
items.strategy: Use independent coroots and the row-coroot convention alpha_j(h_i)=a_ij. Specify labels including zero. P may contain a non-discrete complementary complex subspace; do not identify it with a finite-type weight lattice.
source_locators: Kleshchev §10.1 p127; Perrin Definition 10.5.1 p89

references.title: Kleshchev, Lectures on Infinite Dimensional Lie Algebras
Perrin, Introduction to Kac-Moody Groups and Lie Algebras

items.title: Integrable kac moody module
items.statement: A g(A)-module is integrable if it is a weight module and every e_i and f_i is locally nilpotent. The zero module qualifies; no finite-dimensional weight-space condition is imposed.
items.strategy: Reuse only the weight-module part of the published category-O definition. State local nilpotence vectorwise, with a bound depending on vector and generator. Neither O support nor integrality is part of the definition.
source_locators: Kleshchev §3.1 p38; Perrin §5.2.1 p42

references.title: Kleshchev, Lectures on Infinite Dimensional Lie Algebras
Perrin, Introduction to Kac-Moody Groups and Lie Algebras

items.title: Integrability can be checked on simple root sl2 subalgebras
items.statement: For a weight module V, integrability is equivalent to local finiteness of every simple triple span(e_i,h_i,f_i).
items.strategy: For weight vector v, PBW reordering in three generators follows directly from [h,e]=2e,[h,f]=-2f,[e,f]=h and spans U(sl2)v by f^a e^b v. There are finitely many b by e nilpotence, and then finitely many a for each e^b v by f nilpotence. Finite sums of weight vectors give local finiteness. Conversely finite invariant cyclic spaces have finitely many h eigenvalues inherited from a weight module; e,f shift by ±2, so long enough powers vanish. No appeal to unavailable finite-dimensional complete reducibility is needed.
source_locators: Kleshchev Proposition 3.1.4 pp38–39 (local-finiteness portion); Perrin §5.2.1 p42

references.title: Kleshchev, Lectures on Infinite Dimensional Lie Algebras
Perrin, Introduction to Kac-Moody Groups and Lie Algebras

items.title: Dominance is necessary for an integrable highest weight module
items.statement: Every nonzero integrable highest-weight module of weight lambda, in particular L_A(lambda), has lambda in Pplus. Its highest vector obeys f_i^{lambda(h_i)+1}v=0 and f_i^k v!=0 for 0<=k<=lambda(h_i).
items.strategy: Derive e f^m v=m(lambda(h_i)-m+1)f^{m-1}v by induction from the triple relations already read. Choose the least positive N with f^N v=0. Since f^{N-1}v!=0, N(lambda(h_i)-N+1)=0 forces lambda(h_i)=N-1. This includes label zero and proves the exact terminal power, without semisimplicity.
source_locators: Kleshchev Lemma 10.1.1 p127; Perrin Lemmas 10.5.2,10.5.5 p89

references.title: Kleshchev, Lectures on Infinite Dimensional Lie Algebras
Perrin, Introduction to Kac-Moody Groups and Lie Algebras

items.title: Simple root power relations generate the integrable quotient
items.statement: For lambda in Pplus, let N be the sum of submodules of M_A(lambda) generated by f_i^{lambda(h_i)+1}v. The quotient M_A(lambda)/N is nonzero, highest weight, and integrable.
items.strategy: The triple identity makes each displayed vector killed by e_i; e_j for j!=i commutes with f_i and kills v. It is singular of strictly lower weight, so its generated module has only lower weights by PBW, and their finite sum misses the top. Quotient raising powers vanish from bounded support. For lowering, the published Weyl-automorphism proof step1 establishes ad f_i locally nilpotent on every generator and hence U(g) via the derivation binomial rule; for any word u use f_i^N u=sum_k binom(N,k)(ad f_i)^k(u) f_i^{N-k}. The bounded adjoint powers on u and imposed power on v kill every summand for sufficiently large N. State the binomial identity and inductive proof locally. No Serre-generation or integrability conclusion is assumed.
source_locators: Kleshchev Lemmas 3.1.2–3.1.3 pp37–38 and §10.1 p127; Perrin Lemma 10.5.2 p89

references.title: Kleshchev, Lectures on Infinite Dimensional Lie Algebras
Perrin, Introduction to Kac-Moody Groups and Lie Algebras

items.title: Integrability criterion for simple highest weight kac moody modules
items.statement: For every finite GCM and every lambda in h*, L_A(lambda) is integrable exactly when lambda is dominant integral.
items.strategy: Necessity is the preceding terminal-power argument. For sufficiency, the proper power-generated N lies in the unique maximal proper submodule. Thus L is a quotient of the nonzero integrable quotient; local nilpotence descends, and the weight decomposition descends by finite interpolation. No symmetrizability needed here.
source_locators: Kleshchev Lemma 10.1.1 p127; Perrin Lemma 10.5.2 p89

references.title: Kleshchev, Lectures on Infinite Dimensional Lie Algebras
Perrin, Introduction to Kac-Moody Groups and Lie Algebras

items.title: Integrable weight sets and multiplicities are weyl invariant
items.statement: In any integrable module, each simple reflection gives an isomorphism V_mu -> V_{s_i mu}, so W preserves support and weight-space dimensions, without a finite-multiplicity assumption.
items.strategy: Define T_i=exp(f_i)exp(-e_i)exp(f_i), all series vectorwise finite and invertible. On a finite cyclic sl2 space, the finite conjugation identity exp(X)Y exp(-X)=exp(ad X)Y follows by differentiating the polynomial expression (or coefficient binomial identity); extend it to h using its scalar commuting part. The same explicit triple calculation as the published adjoint lift gives T_i h T_i^{-1}=h-alpha_i(h)h_i. Hence T_i maps each full Cartan weight space bijectively to its reflected space. Products implement each Weyl word; independence of lift from word is not claimed. This proves dimension equality via actual isomorphism even when dimensions are not finite.
source_locators: Kleshchev Proposition 3.2.3 pp40–41; Perrin §5.2.2 pp42–44 and Corollary 10.5.3 p89

references.title: Kleshchev, Lectures on Infinite Dimensional Lie Algebras
Perrin, Introduction to Kac-Moody Groups and Lie Algebras

items.title: Real coroot signs, word length and inversion sets
items.statement: For a finite GCM realization let real coroots be W{h_i}. Positive real coroots have nonnegative integral coordinates in the independent h_i; negative means the opposite. Let length(w) be the least length of a simple-reflection word. Set Inv(w)={beta positive real coroot: w beta is negative} and N(lambda)={beta positive real coroot: lambda(beta)<0} for integral lambda. The following lemma proves the asserted signs and finiteness of Inv(w).
items.strategy: Transpose A and exchange the independent root/coroot families: (h*, {h_i}, {alpha_i}) realizes A transpose. Its Weyl action on h is the dual of the original action, with the same word relations and minimal lengths. Apply the published general GCM root results to this realization. The coroot span has unique integral coordinates. Pairings of integral lambda with it are real integers; complementary complex Cartan values play no role.

references.title: Kleshchev, Lectures on Infinite Dimensional Lie Algebras, Lemmas3.3.1–3.3.3 and Proposition3.4.1(i)–(iii), pp42–44,47

items.title: Reduced words, root signs and finite coroot inversions
items.statement: Each real root and coroot has one sign; a simple reflection permutes the positive real roots other than its own simple root, and likewise for coroots. If w(alpha_i)<0, any word for w admits deletion of one factor in a word for w s_i. Hence length(w s_i)<length(w) iff w(alpha_i)<0, with the corresponding dual-coroot assertion. Every Inv(w) is finite, of cardinality at most length(w).
items.strategy: The published root-space proposition gives one-sign roots, only plus/minus alpha_i on its simple line, and positivity preservation off alpha_i; the published Weyl automorphisms give invariance. For a word w=s_i1...s_it with w alpha_i negative, track suffix images of alpha_i from right to left. At the first positive-to-negative step the positive root must be alpha_is. Put v=s_i(s+1)...s_it, so v alpha_i=alpha_is. Lift v by the published Lie automorphisms. They map the bracket line [g_alpha_i,g_-alpha_i]=C h_i onto C h_is; preservation of the pairing value2 fixes the scalar, so v h_i=h_is. Therefore v s_i v^-1=s_is on the full realization, and w s_i is the original word with s_is deleted. Apply this to a minimal word. If w alpha_i is positive, (w s_i)alpha_i is negative and deletion in the reverse direction proves the strict opposite length inequality. Repeat the entire argument for the transpose realization, whose dual Weyl group has the same length. Each simple coroot reflection changes the sign of only h_i, so composing one reflection changes inversion cardinality by at most1; induction on a word proves finiteness and the bound. No Coxeter presentation or finite Weyl group is assumed.

references.title: Kleshchev, Lectures on Infinite Dimensional Lie Algebras, Lemmas3.3.1–3.3.3 and Proposition3.4.1(i)–(iii), pp42–44,47

items.title: Dominant representatives, wall stabilizers and terminating reflection descent
items.statement: An integral Weyl orbit meeting Pplus has a unique dominant representative eta. Its stabilizer is generated exactly by the simple reflections s_i with eta(h_i)=0. Starting at any weight in this orbit, repeated reflections at any negative simple label terminate at eta; choose the least such index for a deterministic algorithm. No claim is made that every integral orbit meets Pplus.
items.strategy: If lambda=w eta with eta dominant, any positive coroot beta with lambda(beta)<0 must have w^-1 beta negative, so N(lambda) is contained in finite Inv(w^-1). When lambda(h_i)<0, s_i permutes the other positive real coroots and reverses h_i, so |N(s_i lambda)|=|N(lambda)|-1. If no simple label is negative, every positive coroot pairs nonnegatively, hence N is empty. This proves termination. For uniqueness and stabilizers, suppose eta,zeta=w eta are dominant and w=s_i1...s_it is reduced with t>0. The dual length lemma makes w h_it negative. Thus 0<=eta(h_it)=zeta(w h_it)<=0, so s_it fixes eta. Delete that last factor and induct. All deleted factors have zero eta-label, and the endpoint is eta. Conversely each zero-label reflection fixes eta directly. This proves the full parabolic stabilizer formula, not just nonuniqueness of transporting words.

references.title: Kleshchev, Lectures on Infinite Dimensional Lie Algebras, Lemmas3.3.1–3.3.3 and Proposition3.4.1(i)–(iii), pp42–44,47

items.title: Every integrable weight is weyl conjugate toward the dominant chamber
items.statement: For an integral weight of an integrable module whose Weyl orbit meets Pplus, successive reflections at negative simple labels terminate at its unique dominant representative eta. Stab_W(eta) is generated by the zero-label simple reflections; transporting elements need not be unique. Every weight orbit of an integrable highest-weight module, and more generally an integrable category-O module, meets Pplus.
items.strategy: Apply the local chamber lemma for the conditional orbit and full wall-stabilizer claims. For the highest-weight/category-O case, the existing Weyl weight-space isomorphisms preserve support. Reflecting at an integral negative simple label increases the weight by a positive integer multiple of that simple root. The category-O definition gives only finitely many support weights above the starting weight, so this process terminates at a weight with all labels nonnegative. The original conditional and highest-weight claims and the full stabilizer formula are retained. No finite DG root-system page is used.
source_locators: Kleshchev Proposition 3.4.1 pp47–48 and Corollary 10.1.3 p128; Perrin Corollary 10.5.4 p89

references.title: Kleshchev, Lectures on Infinite Dimensional Lie Algebras
Perrin, Introduction to Kac-Moody Groups and Lie Algebras

items.title: An integrable o module is generated by dominant maximal weights
items.statement: Every maximal support weight of a nonzero integrable O-module is dominant integral, and a nonzero vector at that weight generates an integrable highest-weight quotient of its Verma module. More generally every primitive vector has dominant integral weight, and primitive vectors generate as an n-minus module. Generation is by maximal weights in the relevant subquotients, not only globally maximal weights of V.
items.strategy: A maximal weight vector is killed by each positive generator, and its cyclic module inherits integrability. Universality gives the Verma quotient and terminal powers give dominance. For a primitive vector use its nonzero highest class in a quotient; integrability descends and the same argument gives dominance there. Use the exact published primitive-vector generation lemma, whose induction is on the finite upper support set. Do not assert V is generated by its globally maximal support spaces: already L(2) direct sum L(0) for A1 contradicts that reading.
source_locators: Kleshchev Lemma 9.1.3 p118, Theorem 10.4.2 p135; Perrin Proposition 10.3.6 p87 and Lemma 10.5.5 p89

references.title: Kleshchev, Lectures on Infinite Dimensional Lie Algebras
Perrin, Introduction to Kac-Moody Groups and Lie Algebras

items.title: Casimir separates comparable dominant primitive weights
items.statement: For symmetrizable A, an integrable O-module decomposes into generalized eigenspaces for the restricted Casimir; in each summand its primitive weights form an antichain for the positive-root order.
items.strategy: Omega preserves weight spaces. Avoid an undeclared fundamental theorem of algebra: for weight mu the defining Casimir formula gives (Omega-c(mu))v=2 sum_{alpha>0,s} y_{alpha,s}x_{alpha,s}v, a finite sum of negative-root actions on vectors of strictly higher support weights. Induct on the finite upper support set and commute Omega through those root actions to obtain an annihilating polynomial for v that is a product of linear factors (t-c(eta)). Bezout polynomials for the finitely many relatively prime powers (t-a)^N give unique generalized-eigenvector components of v; prove this elementary identity by polynomial division, and use uniqueness to make the decomposition compatible as the annihilating polynomial grows. Hence V is the algebraic direct sum of its generalized eigenspaces. Centrality makes the global generalized eigenspaces submodules. Any primitive highest class of weight lambda in the a-summand is both annihilated by a power of Omega-a and an eigenvector of eigenvalue c(lambda)=(lambda+2rho,lambda), so c(lambda)=a. If dominant lambda>mu, write lambda-mu=sum n_i alpha_i. Then c(lambda)-c(mu)=sum n_i d_i(lambda(h_i)+mu(h_i)+2)>0, because d_i>0 and some n_i>0. Thus comparable distinct primitive weights cannot share a Casimir summand. The published rho convention and d_i normalization are used, not a positive-definite full Cartan form.
source_locators: Kleshchev Lemma 10.4.1 and Theorem 10.4.2 pp134–135; Perrin Lemma 10.6.1 pp89–90 and §11.1

references.title: Kleshchev, Lectures on Infinite Dimensional Lie Algebras
Perrin, Introduction to Kac-Moody Groups and Lie Algebras

items.title: Complete reducibility of integrable kac moody o modules
items.statement: Assume AC and A symmetrizable. Every integrable module V in the published finite-cone, finite-weight-space category O is an algebraic direct sum of L_A(lambda), lambda dominant integral; zero is the empty sum.
items.strategy: Work in a Casimir generalized eigensummand. Every singular cyclic module is simple: a proper nonzero submodule has a maximal weight mu<lambda, giving forbidden comparable primitive weights. Choose a basis of each singular weight space using AC on the set-indexed family of nonempty sets of finite ordered bases. The generated simple modules form a direct sum: a finite relation gives a nonzero kernel of the map from their finite external direct sum; its maximal weight vector is singular; every simple summand has only its top singular line, and the chosen top vectors are independent at each weight, contradiction. Let S be their sum. If V/S!=0, lift a maximal quotient weight vector v of weight mu. It is primitive, and e_i v lies in S. If any e_i v!=0, a simple summand containing that weight has highest lambda>=mu+alpha_i, contradicting the primitive antichain; otherwise v is singular and already lies in S. Thus S=V. Reassemble the canonical Casimir summands. No unproved splitting or general semisimple-module theorem is imported.
source_locators: Kleshchev Lemma 10.4.1, Theorem 10.4.2 pp134–135; Perrin Lemma 10.6.1 pp89–90

references.title: Kleshchev, Lectures on Infinite Dimensional Lie Algebras
Perrin, Introduction to Kac-Moody Groups and Lie Algebras

items.title: Tensor products of integrable highest weight modules decompose
items.statement: Assume AC, A symmetrizable, lambda and mu dominant integral. L_A(lambda) tensor L_A(mu) is integrable, belongs to O, and is a direct sum of dominant highest-weight simples with finite multiplicity of each simple and finite multiplicities at each weight.
items.strategy: Define diagonal action x(v tensor w)=xv tensor w+v tensor xw; expansion of commutators verifies it is a representation. On any elementary tensor, the two summands for e_i commute and each is locally nilpotent, so a sufficiently large binomial power is zero; same for f_i and finite sums. Weights add. At weight lambda+mu-beta only finitely many decompositions beta=beta1+beta2 in Qplus exist, coordinatewise 0<=beta1_i<=beta_i, and the factor spaces are finite dimensional; hence the tensor belongs to O. Apply complete reducibility. A simple copy with highest nu contributes one independent top vector at nu, bounding its multiplicity by the finite dimension of the tensor weight space. Do not claim a closed LR formula.
source_locators: Kleshchev Corollary 10.4.3 p136; Perrin Fact 10.1.2 p85

references.title: Kleshchev, Lectures on Infinite Dimensional Lie Algebras
Perrin, Introduction to Kac-Moody Groups and Lie Algebras

items.title: Affine central coroot from the transpose null ray
items.statement: For an indecomposable affine GCM in row-coroot convention, the unique primitive positive integer b in ker(A^t) defines c_A=sum b_i h_i, a nonzero central element of the derived algebra. On a cyclic highest-weight module c_A acts as lambda(c_A); this defines intrinsic GCM level.
items.strategy: Use the published trichotomy positive transpose null ray and rank n-1. Rational Gaussian elimination yields a rational generator, whose sign is made positive, denominators cleared, and coordinates divided by their gcd. Primitivity makes its positive integer normalization unique. Independence of the h_i gives c_A!=0. Relations give [c_A,e_j]=(sum b_i a_ij)e_j=0, similarly f_j, and [c_A,h]=0. It belongs to the derived algebra because h_i=[e_i,f_i]. Commuting c_A through each finite enveloping word applied to the highest vector proves scalar action. No loop model, degree, null-root normalization, or arbitrary-index choice enters.
source_locators: Kleshchev §6.1 pp77–78 and §11.1 p144; complete local proof in phase-2-next-20-affine-level-local-resolution.md

items.title: Integrable affine highest weights have nonnegative integral level
items.statement: A dominant integral highest weight for an indecomposable affine GCM has nonnegative integer intrinsic level. Every nonzero highest-weight module of positive level, in particular its integrable simple, is infinite dimensional.
items.strategy: The level is sum b_i lambda(h_i), with both factors nonnegative integers. If a positive-level highest-weight module had finite dimension, scalar central action would give tr(c_A)=lambda(c_A)dim V!=0. But c_A=sum b_i[e_i,f_i] and finite matrices have tr(EF)=tr(FE), proved by exchanging their two finite indices, so the trace is zero. This supplies the complete positive-level argument independently of RL13 and Weyl–Kac.
source_locators: Kleshchev §11.1, Proposition 11.1.1 p144; local trace proof in phase-2-next-20-affine-level-local-resolution.md

items.title: Level zero integrable affine highest weight simples are one dimensional
items.statement: An irreducible integrable affine highest-weight module of intrinsic level zero is one dimensional and the derived algebra acts trivially. Complementary Cartan directions may have nonzero scalar action.
items.strategy: Positive b_i and nonnegative integral simple labels with weighted sum zero force each label zero. The exact rank-one terminal-power argument gives f_i v=0. All e_i kill v by highest weight, and all h act scalarly, so Cv is invariant under the generators and hence equals the cyclic module. All commutators act trivially on a one-dimensional representation. Preserve the complementary Cartan scalars; do not identify this with the trivial full-affine representation.
source_locators: Kleshchev Proposition 11.1.1 p144 (character-based original); independent local rank-one proof in phase-2-next-20-affine-level-local-resolution.md

title: Integrable Highest Weight Kac Moody Modules — Examples

items.title: Integrable highest weight modules for rank one gcm
items.statement: For A=[2] and highest label m>=0, L_A(m) has basis v_0,...,v_m with h v_k=(m-2k)v_k, f v_k=v_{k+1}, e v_k=k(m-k+1)v_{k-1}, and absent endpoint vectors zero.
items.strategy: Check [h,e]=2e,[h,f]=-2f,[e,f]=h on all basis vectors including k=0,m. The formulas give nilpotent e,f and a cyclic top v_0. Any nonzero invariant subspace has a weight vector v_k by distinct h weights; e^k sends it to a nonzero multiple of v_0 and successive f generate the whole space. This proves simplicity and universality identifies L_A(m). The finite rank-one algebra follows directly from the three-generator relations, with no missing DG finite-type equivalence theorem.
source_locators: Kleshchev §10.1 p127 and §3.1 pp37–39

references.title: Kleshchev, Lectures on Infinite Dimensional Lie Algebras
Perrin, Introduction to Kac-Moody Groups and Lie Algebras

items.title: The basic level one weight of affine sl2
items.statement: For A=[[2,-2],[-2,2]], choose Lambda_0(h_0)=1,Lambda_0(h_1)=0 and any fixed complementary Cartan value. Then Lambda_0 is dominant integral, c_A=h_0+h_1, its level is one, and L_A(Lambda_0) is integrable and infinite dimensional.
items.strategy: The displayed matrix has primitive positive left null vector (1,1), so it is affine by the positive-vector characterization. Extend the two prescribed labels across a finite Cartan basis. Sum them to obtain level one, then apply integrability and the finite-trace contradiction. This is an intrinsic GCM example only; no loop-cocycle normalization or construction of its weight layers is asserted.
source_locators: Kleshchev §6.1 pp77–78 and §11.1 p144; affine-level-local-resolution.md

items.title: Simple root string in an integrable kac moody module
items.statement: For a nonzero i-highest weight vector v of weight eta in an integrable module with eta(h_i)=m, the cyclic simple-root string is v,f_i v,...,f_i^m v, with weights eta-k alpha_i and reflection k -> m-k.
items.strategy: Use the terminal-power proof on the single triple (only e_i v=0 is required) to derive m in Z>=0 and the exact m+1 nonzero-independent string. The commutator formula gives e_i f_i^k v=k(m-k+1)f_i^{k-1}v, and s_i(eta-k alpha_i)=eta-(m-k)alpha_i. Distinguish a cyclic finite string from the entire intersection of an arbitrary integrable module support with eta+Z alpha_i, which can be infinite.
source_locators: Kleshchev Proposition 3.1.4 pp38–39 and §3.2 pp39–41

items.title: A kac moody verma module is not integrable in general
items.statement: A nonzero-rank Kac–Moody Verma module is not integrable: for any simple index i, f_i^N v_lambda is nonzero for every N>=0, including dominant integral lambda.
items.strategy: The simple negative root vector is a nonzero element of its one-dimensional root space. Include it in the ordered homogeneous PBW basis; its arbitrary powers are distinct independent monomials in U(n-minus), hence nonzero on the free highest generator. Thus f_i is not locally nilpotent on that vector. A=[2],lambda=0 is a concrete witness.
source_locators: Kleshchev §9.1 pp116–117; Perrin Proposition 10.3.2(ii) p86

references.title: Kleshchev, Lectures on Infinite Dimensional Lie Algebras
Perrin, Introduction to Kac-Moody Groups and Lie Algebras

items.title: Local nilpotence of only the ei does not imply integrability
items.statement: In M_A(lambda), every simple raising operator is locally nilpotent but no simple lowering operator is locally nilpotent on its highest vector; therefore the raising half alone does not imply integrability.
items.strategy: On weight lambda-beta with beta=sum b_j alpha_j in Qplus, e_i^N has weight lambda-beta+N alpha_i, absent when N>b_i. For a finite sum of weight vectors take the maximum of finitely many b_i. The preceding PBW witness provides the failing lowering half, even at lambda=0 in rank one.
source_locators: Kleshchev §9.1 pp116–117 and §10.1 p127; Perrin Lemma 10.5.2 p89
